title: Photosynthesis Explained (sample transcript for local testing)

segments.text: Hi everyone, today we are going to learn how plants make their own food through a process called photosynthesis.
Photosynthesis happens mainly in the leaves, inside tiny structures called chloroplasts. Chloroplasts contain a green pigment called chlorophyll.
Chlorophyll absorbs sunlight, mostly red and blue light. It reflects green light, which is why leaves look green to us.
The plant needs three things: sunlight, water absorbed by the roots, and carbon dioxide which enters through small pores on the leaf called stomata.
Using the energy from sunlight, the plant converts carbon dioxide and water into glucose, which is a sugar, and releases oxygen as a by-product.
The overall equation is: six carbon dioxide plus six water, in the presence of light, gives one glucose plus six oxygen.
Photosynthesis has two stages. The first is the light-dependent reactions, which happen in the thylakoid membranes and produce ATP and NADPH.
The second stage is the Calvin cycle, which happens in the stroma. It uses ATP and NADPH to fix carbon dioxide into glucose. It does not need light directly.
The glucose is used by the plant for energy, or stored as starch, or used to build cellulose for cell walls.
That's it for today. In the next video we will look at respiration, which is kind of the reverse of photosynthesis. Thanks for watching!
